issues.legal_issue: Applications for probate or letters of administration made to a civil court are subject to the limitation regime applicable to applications for which no other period is prescribed.
material_facts: The respondents applied to a civil court under the Indian Succession Act for letters of administration.
The courts below disagreed about whether the application was subject to Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
issues.conclusion: Article 137 applies to an application for probate or letters of administration made to a civil court.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963 applies to any petition or application filed under an Act in a civil court, and provides a three-year period running from when the right to apply accrues. The Court relied on The Kerala State Electricity Board, Trivandrum v. T.P. Kunhaliumma, which held that Article 137 is not confined to applications under the Code of Civil Procedure. Sections 264 and 2(bb) of the Indian Succession Act establish that the relevant application is made to the District Judge as a civil court.

predicates.probate_or_administration_application_to: An applicant seeks probate or letters of administration from a civil court.

issues.definition: When an applicant seeks probate or letters of administration from a civil court, the application is subject to a limitation period.

issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for an application for letters of administration begins when the right to apply accrues, and the application is timely when filed within that period after the triggering event.
material_facts: A prior petition for probate concerning the same will was withdrawn, and the respondents were given liberty to initiate appropriate proceedings.
The respondents filed their application for letters of administration within three years after the prior petition was withdrawn.
The Court held that the right to apply arose when the prior petition was withdrawn, rather than automatically on the testator’s death.
issues.conclusion: The application was within time because it was filed within three years after the right to apply accrued upon withdrawal of the prior probate petition.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, the three-year period runs from when the right to apply accrues. An application for probate or letters of administration seeks the court’s recognition to perform a duty and constitutes a continuing right; the right to apply arises when it becomes necessary to apply, not necessarily on the deceased’s death. The Court accepted the continuing-right reasoning in Vasudev Daulatram Sadarangani v. Sajni Prem Lalwani, while rejecting that case’s conclusion that the right necessarily accrues on death. It also referred to S. Krishnaswami v. E. Ramiah on the nature of the proceedings and relied on the circumstances of the earlier petition’s withdrawal to identify when the right accrued here.

rule.if: probate_or_administration_application and earlier_probate_petition_withdrawn and liberty_to_start_proceedings_granted and application_filed_within_three_years_of_withdrawal

predicates.probate_or_administration_application: An applicant seeks probate or letters of administration from a court.
predicates.earlier_probate_petition_withdrawn: A person who previously sought probate concerning the same testamentary instrument withdrew that petition.
predicates.liberty_to_start_proceedings_granted: The court permitted the persons seeking the later application to initiate appropriate proceedings.
predicates.application_filed_within_three_years_of_: The later applicant filed within three years after the earlier probate petition was withdrawn.

issues.definition: When a probate or administration application follows withdrawal of an earlier probate petition, liberty to start proceedings was granted, and the later application was filed within three years of withdrawal, the application is timely.
